purpose.statement: Place a learner onto suitable BreadTrans learning content by measuring four skills with task types appropriate to each.
purpose.decisionReversibility: Fully reversible - a learner may move between content freely at any time.
purpose.targetPopulation: Vietnamese students and university students, approximately 16-24, general English.
purpose.notAnExamination: Not a certification instrument. No CEFR, ALTE or exam-equivalence claim (see research doc).

constructBoundary.basis: CEFR Companion Volume communicative model: reception, production, interaction and mediation, each with spoken and written modes. Listening/Reading/Speaking/Writing remain recognisable within reception and production, so the learner-facing organisation stays the four skills.

mapping.Listening: reception - spoken (requires audio playback; the script must not be readable before answering)
mapping.Speaking: production - spoken (requires a learner audio recording)

constructBoundary.LanguageUse: Auxiliary diagnostic dimension only. Grammar/vocabulary items are reported in the profile but carry weight 0 in the overall placement, so they can never substitute for a skill measurement.
constructBoundary.interactionAndMediation: Not implemented as modules. The framework contains them, but they are not required by this placement purpose. Task design should still recognise that communicative competence is broader than four isolated skill labels.

formLengthRationale: Weir's stakes-proportionality (Cambridge socio-cognitive framework): the higher the stakes the stricter the evidential demands. This is a low-stakes, fully reversible placement decision inside a learning product, so a ~40 minute form is proportionate. A certification-length instrument would add learner fatigue and grading cost without improving the routing decision it informs.

scoring.withinSkillItemWeighting: equal, and disclosed to the learner
scoring.withinSkillBasis: British Council Aptis TR/2015/001 - all items in a receptive paper equally weighted, disclosed in advance. This source speaks to weighting WITHIN a paper only.
scoring.overallWeightRationale: Not equal-by-default. Two reasons, both evidential. (1) Reliability of evidence: each receptive skill carries 10 objectively keyed items, while Speaking carries 2 rubric-graded tasks and Writing 1. Giving a single AI-graded writing task the same influence as ten keyed reading items would let the noisiest measurement move placement as much as the most reliable one. (2) Construct coverage still matters: the legacy form had zero productive evidence, so productive skills retain a combined 40% - enough that a learner who cannot produce language is not placed as though they can. Receptive 60 / productive 40 is the deliberate compromise between measurement reliability and construct validity.
scoring.overallFormula: round((L + R + S + W) / 4), computed ONLY when Listening, Reading, Speaking and Writing are all COMPLETE. While any required skill is incomplete the overall figure is null - it is never computed over the subset that happens to be finished, and never represented as 0.
scoring.compensatoryBasis: Cambridge English socio-cognitive framework reports skills separately while treating overall ability as compensatory. This supports the compensatory form of the secondary figure, not any particular cross-skill split.
scoring.weakSkillPolicy: The per-skill profile is the primary output, so a weak skill is visible as its own band and drives recommendations. The secondary overall figure stays compensatory and is never presented as the sole result.
scoring.roundingRule: Math.round, applied once per skill score and once to the overall figure. No double rounding.

minimumEvidence.objectiveSkill: a skill reports a percentage only when it has at least 3 scored items
minimumEvidence.productiveSkill: a skill reports a percentage only when every one of its tasks reached GRADED

scoring.pendingSkillRule: If any of Listening/Reading/Speaking/Writing is not COMPLETE the attempt is PENDING_GRADING: the per-skill results available so far are shown, and the overall figure and placement band are withheld (null). No partial overall is ever calculated.
scoring.failedGradingRule: If a productive task reaches GRADING_FAILED the attempt is PARTIAL. The affected skill reports no score, the overall figure is withheld, and the learner is offered a retry. A failed grading never scores 0 and never silently finalizes a placement.
scoring.primaryResultNote: The four per-skill bands are the primary result. BreadTrans content is organised per skill, so four bands are directly actionable; a single number is not the product output.
scoring.weightingRationale: Three options were compared (equal 25/25/25/25; 30/30/20/20; skill-profile-first with a separate overall) against construct validity, observations per skill, rubric and AI grading uncertainty, learner interpretation, receptive-masking risk and productive-task variance. 30/30/20/20 was REJECTED: its only argument was that more objective items implies more reliability implies more weight, but item count is not reliability without discrimination and distribution evidence, and it downweights exactly the two skills the legacy form could not measure. Skill-profile-first was chosen: the four bands are the primary result, which confines rubric noise to the affected skill and makes a weak productive skill visible instead of masked. The secondary overall figure uses EQUAL weighting because, absent reliability evidence, equal weights assert the least - any unequal split would claim we know which skill our instrument measures better. No external source decides this split; Cambridge supports a compensatory overall and Aptis supports equal weighting within a paper, neither prescribes a cross-skill split.
scoring.weightingNotDerivedFrom: Not derived from Cambridge or Aptis. Those sources support compensatory overall scoring and equal item weighting within a paper only. Cambridge products use a range of weighting arrangements including equal skill weighting.
scoring.knownWeakness: With a single Writing task the Writing band is the least stable of the four. Adding a second Writing task is the first change to evaluate once pilot data exists.

levelSystem.boundaryRationale: The legacy two-boundary scale (45 / 75) is retained at its lower edge for continuity with existing learner history, and one additional upper band is added because V2 measures a wider ability range than a 20-item MCQ screen could. Boundaries are routing thresholds for content difficulty, not proficiency claims.
levelSystem.cefrClaimBasis: BreadTrans V2 does not yet have sufficient empirical and standard-setting evidence to make a defensible CEFR-linked placement claim. The Council of Europe Manual (2009) does provide for relating examinations to the CEFR, through familiarisation, specification, standardisation/benchmarking, standard setting and validation. BreadTrans has run none of the evidence-side procedures (no standard-setting panel, no item calibration, no candidate sample, no reliability study, no external validation), so no CEFR wording ships with V2.
levelSystem.learnerFacingWording: Describe the output as a placement indication used to route learning content. Never as a certified or CEFR level.

mediaPolicy.listeningAudio: Authored for V2 via the project's existing Azure Speech pipeline. Versioned storage keys under a V2-specific prefix. Script hash and audio hash recorded per item so the audio-to-script binding is provable rather than inferred from a filename.
mediaPolicy.transcriptPrivacy: The authoritative script must not reach the client before the learner answers that item.

requiredBeforeActivation: all four skills present with their blueprint item counts
every Listening item has a verified audio asset (bytes > 0, decodes, duration plausible, script hash matches)
every productive task has a rubric with a rubricVersion
scoringVersion and blueprintVersion present on the assessment
no invalid answer key (correctIndex within range)
no duplicate item prompt and no duplicate audio asset
no Listening item left SEMANTIC_AMBIGUOUS or SEMANTIC_MISMATCH

legacyPolicy.legacyFormPreserved: The 20-item form (assessment id 1) is not rewritten, not repurposed and not deleted.
legacyPolicy.legacyAttempts: Historical attempts keep their own assessment and scoring version and are never rescored with the V2 scorer.
legacyPolicy.activation: V2 becomes current only through an explicit authoritative active flag, never by being the highest id.

expectedCompletionMinutesNote: Recalculated from the matrix after adding the second Writing task (+16 min of Writing instead of 10) and reducing LanguageUse to 5 items. Not measured with real users. At this length, measured abandonment per section is the first validation item to watch - see the psychometric validation backlog.

validationStatus.currentState: neither complete; engineering not started beyond research + blueprint

objectiveItemAnalysis: distractor performance - distractors chosen by nobody or by stronger learners
internal consistency per receptive skill where item count supports it
answer-key confirmation against live response data
score distribution per skill and overall (floor/ceiling effects)
skill-score correlations - do the four skills behave as distinguishable constructs
productiveTaskAnalysis: grading consistency across repeated submissions of the same response
human-vs-AI agreement on a validation sample (exact and adjacent)
score drift across provider and model versions - re-score a fixed sample on every provider/model change and alert on movement
rubric dimension behaviour - redundant or non-discriminating dimensions
rubric-version comparability when a rubric changes
boundariesAndOperations: boundary stability - learners sitting within a few points of a band edge
test-retest or parallel-form evidence if a second form becomes feasible
measured completion time: median, P75, P90, per-section
device split (mobile vs desktop) for recording and writing tasks
ifCefrLinkageWanted: run the Council of Europe Manual procedures in order before any CEFR wording appears

difficultyScale.purpose: An authoring-side relative difficulty scale for ITEMS. It exists so content can carry a deliberate progression without borrowing a proficiency vocabulary. It is not a proficiency scale, is not calibrated against any learner data, and is never shown to a learner.
difficultyScale.notCefr: D1-D4 are NOT CEFR levels and are not derived from any CEFR conversion. They were assigned from the intended relative progression of the previous draft, not by translating A2/B1/B2.
difficultyScale.notResultBands: Deliberately separate from the result bands (Starter/Foundation/Intermediate/Upper). Result bands describe a learner OUTCOME; D1-D4 describe an ITEM. No mapping between the two exists or should be inferred.

tiers.label: most accessible
tiers.intent: short, high-frequency language; the answer is directly available once the text or audio is understood

tiers.label: straightforward
tiers.intent: requires locating a specific piece of information among competing nearby details

tiers.label: demanding
tiers.intent: requires reading or hearing past the literal wording - purpose, attitude, reference, meaning in context

tiers.label: most demanding
tiers.intent: requires combining information or drawing an inference that is not stated

difficultyScale.productiveTasks: Productive tasks carry a difficultyRange rather than a single tier, because one prompt is answered across a span of ability.

itemLevelPolicy.itemDifficultyField: difficultyTier (D1-D4) or difficultyRange for productive tasks
